title: Affine complexes have sheaf Tor amplitude exactly when their module complexes do
statement: Let A be a ring and X = Spec(A) [def-pc-scheme]. Let M^\bullet be a complex of A-modules and let E be the corresponding object of D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)\subseteq D(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-derived-category] under the affine quasi-coherent derived equivalence [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence]. For integers a\le b, the following are equivalent: (i) E has Tor amplitude in [a,b], meaning that H^i(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G)=0 for every \mathcal O_X-module \mathcal G and every i\notin[a,b]; (ii) M^\bullet has Tor amplitude in [a,b], meaning that H^i(M^\bullet\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N)=0 for every A-module N and every i\notin[a,b].

proof.text: Choose a module flat model P in [a,b] using module_torAmplitudeIn_iff_exists_flat_model. BoundedFlatKFlat supplies the acyclicity formulation of K-flatness; isKFlat_tilde therefore makes termwise tilde P K-flat. Transport the derived isomorphism to the termwise tilde of M using the affine equivalence comparison. For any sheaf G, mapBifunctorSingle₂Iso identifies tensor with G in degree zero with termwise tensor. Tilde and tensorRight G preserve zero objects, so the tensor terms, and therefore homology, vanish outside [a,b]. This gives an explicit witness of schemeDerivedTensorCohomologyVanishes.

For the converse take a flat K-flat module resolution s:P to M from the proved generic source exists_quasiIso_flat_kFlat. For each module N and degree i outside [a,b], apply the given sheaf vanishing to tilde N. Unpack its K-flat witness and use kFlat_derivedTensor_comparison_natIso on singleton constant families to deduce zero cohomology of the sheaf derived tensor. The single-complex functor comparison and derivedTensor_tilde_iso identify that tensor with Q of tilde Tot(P tensor N[0]). The module K-flat comparison QObjTensorQObjIsoOfKFlatLeft identifies Q of Tot(P tensor N[0]) with Q(M) tensor-derived N[0].

Apply affineDerivedTilde_homology_comparison to the affine derived equivalence and to the total module tensor complex. This identifies the sheaf cohomology with tilde of the module derived cohomology. Full faithfulness of tilde, from its adjunction with invertible unit, detects the zero identity morphism and hence zero module cohomology. The isGE_iff and isLE_iff characterizations convert vanishing below a and above b to homologyConcentratedIn for every N, which is exactly torAmplitudeIn.
